age.peak: older adults and infants/children; also common in adults 20–60 with limited sun exposure

demographics: More common in people with dark skin living at higher latitudes
More common in exclusively breastfed infants not receiving supplementation
More common in older adults, especially those who are housebound or institutionalized
More common in people with obesity
More common in populations with limited sun exposure due to clothing, indoor work, or northern latitude

risk_factors.text: Limited sun exposure (housebound, northern latitude, covered skin, winter)
Exclusively breastfed infant without vitamin D supplementation
Malabsorption (celiac disease, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, cystic fibrosis)
Gastric bypass or other bariatric surgery
Medications that affect vitamin D metabolism (anticonvulsants, glucocorticoids, cholestyramine, orlistat)
Low dietary intake of vitamin D (little fatty fish, fortified milk, or eggs)

social_history: Wears concealing clothing for cultural or religious reasons

chief_complaints.text: I feel tired all the time
I have pain in my legs and hips
I just don't feel like myself

hpi.onset: Gradual and insidious over weeks to months; often no clear onset
hpi.duration: Usually months to years before diagnosis
hpi.progression: Slowly progressive; may be stable or worsen with continued deficiency
hpi.location: Diffuse; commonly lower back, hips, legs, and ribs
hpi.quality: Dull, deep ache in bones; muscles feel weak and heavy
hpi.severity: Mild to moderate; often 3–5/10, worse with activity
hpi.timing: Constant or worse with activity and weight-bearing

associated_symptoms.text: Muscle weakness, especially in the thighs and shoulders

pertinent_negatives: Muscle pain triggered by exercise and relieved by rest (claudication)

negatives: Morning stiffness lasting more than an hour
Weakness that is focal or one-sided

atypical.how_it_differs: Can present with rickets: bowing of the legs, delayed walking, widened wrists and ankles, and a soft skull. Infants may be irritable and have delayed motor milestones.
missing_classic_features: Bone pain described as an ache
Muscle weakness reported by the patient

atypical.how_it_differs: Exclusively breastfed infants may present with seizures, poor feeding, or breathing difficulty due to low calcium, rather than bone pain.
May present with falls, fractures, or confusion rather than reporting bone pain; symptoms are often attributed to aging.
May present with leg cramps, pelvic girdle pain, or fatigue; routine prenatal vitamins may mask or partially treat it.
Symptoms may be milder or absent despite low vitamin D levels because fat sequesters the vitamin; may present with nonspecific fatigue.
Chronic kidney disease impairs activation of vitamin D; may present with bone pain and fractures out of proportion to sun exposure.

general.mild: Well-appearing, no distress; may look tired
general.moderate: Mildly uncomfortable with movement; slow to rise from a chair
general.severe: Ill-appearing with an antalgic or waddling gait; reluctant to bear weight
general.critical: Distressed, unable to bear weight or stand without support; may have skeletal deformity

findings.maneuver: Press firmly over the sternum, anterior tibia, and ribs
findings.finding: Focal bone tenderness over the sternum, tibia, or ribs

findings.maneuver: Test proximal strength: ask the patient to rise from a chair without using their arms and to resist hip flexion and shoulder abduction
findings.finding: Proximal muscle weakness, especially in the hips and shoulders

findings.maneuver: Observe the patient walking and rising from a chair
findings.finding: Waddling or antalgic gait with difficulty rising from a chair

findings.maneuver: Inspect the long bones and chest wall
findings.finding: Bowing of the legs, widened wrists or ankles, or rachitic rosary (children)

findings.maneuver: Inspect and palpate the joints for swelling, warmth, and redness
findings.finding: No joint swelling, warmth, or redness

findings.maneuver: Test sensation, deep tendon reflexes, and focal strength
findings.finding: No focal weakness, sensory loss, or hyperreflexia

findings.maneuver: Inspect the skin for rash, pallor, or jaundice

labs.caveat: Total calcium is usually normal because of compensatory hyperparathyroidism; low calcium suggests severe or prolonged deficiency, especially in infants and children.
Low phosphorus is more common in children with rickets and in severe deficiency.
Elevated alkaline phosphatase reflects increased bone turnover; can be markedly high in rickets and osteomalacia.
Ordered to exclude hypothyroidism as a cause of fatigue, muscle weakness, and bone pain.
Ordered to exclude B12 deficiency as a cause of fatigue and neurologic symptoms.
Ordered to exclude folate deficiency as a cause of fatigue.
Elevated creatinine suggests chronic kidney disease, which impairs activation of vitamin D and is a common cause of deficiency.
Low albumin suggests malabsorption or chronic illness; total calcium should be corrected for albumin.

imaging.study: X-ray of the affected bones (e.g., wrist, knee, chest)
imaging.preferred_when: Children with suspected rickets or adults with severe bone pain

findings.text: Osteopenia or generalized decreased bone density
Widened growth plates and cupping, fraying, or splaying of the metaphyses (rickets)
Rachitic rosary (beading of the ribs at the costochondral junctions)

imaging.preferred_when: Adults with risk factors for osteoporosis or after treatment

findings.text: Low bone mineral density (osteopenia or osteoporosis)

initial.why: The best test to diagnose vitamin D deficiency; reflects total body vitamin D stores.
Assesses for hypocalcemia, which can occur in severe deficiency.
Low phosphorus supports the diagnosis and is common in rickets.
Elevated alkaline phosphatase indicates increased bone turnover.
Elevated PTH confirms secondary hyperparathyroidism from vitamin D deficiency.
Assesses kidney function, as chronic kidney disease is a common cause and affects management.

supporting.why: Excludes hypothyroidism as a cause of fatigue and muscle weakness.
supporting.only_if: fatigue or muscle weakness is prominent

supporting.why: Excludes B12 deficiency as a cause of fatigue and neurologic symptoms.
supporting.only_if: fatigue or neurologic symptoms are prominent

supporting.why: Excludes folate deficiency as a cause of fatigue.
Assesses nutritional status and helps correct total calcium.
supporting.only_if: malabsorption or chronic illness is suspected

supporting.test: X-ray of the affected bones (e.g., wrist, knee, chest)
supporting.why: Evaluates for rickets or osteomalacia in children or adults with severe bone pain.
supporting.only_if: severe bone pain, deformity, or suspected rickets

supporting.why: Assesses bone mineral density in adults at risk for osteoporosis.
supporting.only_if: adult with risk factors for osteoporosis or after treatment

not_indicated.test: X-ray of the affected bones (e.g., wrist, knee, chest)
not_indicated.why: Not routinely needed for diagnosis; reserved for severe cases or suspected rickets.
Not needed for diagnosis; used for monitoring or assessing osteoporosis risk.
Not routinely needed unless another cause of fatigue is suspected.
Not routinely needed; specific electrolytes are ordered individually.
No role in the workup of vitamin D deficiency.

decision_points: Confirm deficiency with a 25-hydroxyvitamin D level before starting high-dose supplementation.
Check calcium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase, and PTH to assess for metabolic bone disease and secondary hyperparathyroidism.
In children with suspected rickets, obtain wrist or knee x-rays to look for metaphyseal changes.
In adults with severe deficiency or risk factors, consider DXA to assess bone mineral density.
Evaluate for underlying causes such as malabsorption, chronic kidney disease, or medications.

criteria.name: Vitamin D status by 25-hydroxyvitamin D level
criteria.summary: Deficiency is generally defined as a 25-hydroxyvitamin D level below 20 ng/mL. Insufficiency is 20-29 ng/mL. Levels of 30 ng/mL or higher are considered sufficient by many guidelines. Severe deficiency is often defined as below 5 ng/mL.

differential.name: Primary hyperparathyroidism
differential.why_considered: Causes bone pain, muscle weakness, and fatigue with abnormal calcium and vitamin D metabolism
differential.trigger: Elevated calcium with low or low-normal phosphorus and an inappropriately normal or high PTH

exam: Band keratopathy or bone tenderness in severe cases
imaging: Osteopenia or subperiosteal bone resorption on x-ray
Parathyroid adenoma on sestamibi or ultrasound

differential.name: Hypophosphatasia
differential.why_considered: Rare inherited disorder with poor bone mineralization, bone pain, and fractures that mimics osteomalacia
differential.trigger: Low alkaline phosphatase for age with bone pain or fractures

labs: Normal or high calcium and phosphorus

differential.name: Fibromyalgia
differential.why_considered: Chronic widespread pain, fatigue, and muscle aches are common reasons patients are tested for vitamin D deficiency

history: Widespread pain for more than 3 months
Symptoms fluctuate with stress and weather
exam: Multiple tender points or widespread tenderness
labs: Normal calcium, phosphorus, alkaline phosphatase, and PTH

differential.name: Hypothyroidism
differential.why_considered: Fatigue, muscle weakness, muscle aches, and low mood overlap with vitamin D deficiency

exam: Delayed relaxation of deep tendon reflexes

differential.name: Polymyalgia rheumatica
differential.why_considered: Proximal muscle pain and stiffness in older adults can resemble the muscle weakness and bone pain of vitamin D deficiency

history: Abrupt onset of shoulder and hip girdle pain
Morning stiffness lasting more than 45 minutes
Symptoms improve dramatically with low-dose prednisone
exam: Pain with active movement but preserved strength
labs: Normal calcium, phosphorus, and alkaline phosphatase

differential.name: Multiple myeloma
differential.why_considered: Bone pain, fatigue, and osteopenia in older adults can be mistaken for vitamin D deficiency

labs: Elevated total protein with low albumin
Monoclonal protein on serum or urine protein electrophoresis
imaging: Lytic bone lesions on skeletal survey or low-dose whole-body CT

differential.name: Celiac disease
differential.why_considered: Malabsorption causes vitamin D deficiency and can present with bone pain, fatigue, and muscle weakness

imaging: Duodenal biopsy showing villous atrophy and crypt hyperplasia

differential.name: Chronic kidney disease
differential.why_considered: Impaired renal activation of vitamin D causes deficiency and metabolic bone disease

severity.mild: 25-hydroxyvitamin D 10–19 ng/mL; no symptoms or only mild fatigue; normal calcium, phosphorus, and alkaline phosphatase
severity.moderate: 25-hydroxyvitamin D 5–9 ng/mL; bone pain, proximal muscle weakness, fatigue; alkaline phosphatase may be elevated; calcium usually normal
severity.severe: 25-hydroxyvitamin D less than 5 ng/mL; marked bone pain, waddling gait, difficulty rising from a chair, fractures; hypocalcemia and hypophosphatemia may be present; rickets or osteomalacia on imaging
severity.critical: Severe deficiency with symptomatic hypocalcemia (tetany, seizures, laryngospasm, prolonged QT) or life-threatening complications such as cardiomyopathy in infants or severe respiratory muscle weakness

red_flags.meaning: Severe hypocalcemia from prolonged vitamin D deficiency; needs urgent calcium and vitamin D replacement

red_flags.finding: New focal bone pain or pathologic fracture
red_flags.meaning: Osteomalacia with insufficiency fracture or another bone lesion; needs imaging

red_flags.finding: Inability to bear weight or stand from a chair
red_flags.meaning: Severe proximal myopathy; high fall and fracture risk

red_flags.finding: Infant with poor feeding, irritability, or breathing difficulty
red_flags.meaning: Possible hypocalcemic cardiomyopathy or rickets; urgent evaluation

complications.name: Osteoporosis and fragility fractures
clues: Low bone mineral density on DXA

special_populations.differences: Can present with rickets: bowing of the legs, delayed walking, widened wrists and ankles, rachitic rosary, and craniotabes. Alkaline phosphatase is often markedly elevated and phosphorus low.
Exclusively breastfed infants without supplementation are at high risk. May present with seizures, poor feeding, or breathing difficulty from hypocalcemia rather than bone pain.
May present with falls, fractures, or confusion rather than reporting bone pain. Skin makes vitamin D less efficiently and kidneys activate it less well. Higher intake (800 IU/day) is recommended.
May present with leg cramps, pelvic girdle pain, or fatigue. Routine prenatal vitamins may partially treat it. Deficiency is associated with preeclampsia and gestational diabetes.
Body fat sequesters vitamin D, so higher doses are often needed to reach sufficiency. Symptoms may be mild or absent despite low levels.
Chronic kidney disease impairs activation of vitamin D. May need activated vitamin D analogs (calcitriol) rather than plain cholecalciferol. Monitor calcium and phosphorus closely.
Chronic liver disease impairs 25-hydroxylation. May need higher or alternative dosing and monitoring.
Low vitamin D is associated with increased susceptibility to infections; supplementation may be part of supportive care.

key_questions.question: How much time do you spend outdoors in the sun, and do you cover your skin or use sunscreen?
key_questions.looking_for: Limited sun exposure: housebound, indoor or night-shift work, high latitude, concealing clothing, or heavy sunscreen use

key_questions.question: What do you usually eat and drink in a day? Do you drink milk or eat fatty fish, eggs, or fortified foods?
key_questions.looking_for: Low dietary intake of vitamin D from fatty fish, fortified milk, eggs, or supplements

key_questions.question: Do you take any vitamin D or multivitamin supplements?
key_questions.looking_for: No supplementation, or an inadequate dose; breastfed infants without 400 IU daily are at high risk

key_questions.question: Have you had stomach or intestinal surgery, such as gastric bypass?
key_questions.looking_for: Bariatric surgery or small bowel resection, which impairs absorption

key_questions.question: Do you have any conditions that affect absorption, like celiac disease, Crohn's disease, or cystic fibrosis?
Do you have kidney or liver disease?
key_questions.looking_for: Chronic kidney or liver disease, which impairs activation of vitamin D

key_questions.question: Do you take any seizure medicines, steroids, cholesterol medicines, or weight-loss medicines?
key_questions.looking_for: Anticonvulsants, glucocorticoids, cholestyramine, or orlistat that affect vitamin D metabolism

key_questions.question: Have you noticed any bone pain, muscle weakness, or trouble getting up from a chair or climbing stairs?
key_questions.looking_for: Diffuse bone pain and proximal muscle weakness, especially in the hips and shoulders

key_questions.question: Have you had any falls or broken bones with little or no trauma?
key_questions.looking_for: Fragility fractures or falls suggesting osteomalacia or osteoporosis

key_questions.question: Have you had any numbness around the mouth, muscle spasms, or twitching?
key_questions.looking_for: Symptoms of hypocalcemia such as perioral numbness, carpopedal spasm, or tetany

key_questions.question: For infants and children: is the child exclusively breastfed, and are they receiving vitamin D drops?
key_questions.looking_for: Exclusively breastfed infant without 400 IU daily supplementation

key_questions.question: For children: has the child had delayed walking, bowing of the legs, or widened wrists and ankles?
key_questions.looking_for: Signs of rickets such as bowing, delayed motor milestones, or skeletal deformity

reasoning_points: Low 25-hydroxyvitamin D level confirms the diagnosis (deficiency generally below 20 ng/mL)
Risk factors such as limited sun exposure, dark skin, exclusive breastfeeding without supplementation, obesity, malabsorption, or chronic kidney or liver disease
Symptoms of bone pain, proximal muscle weakness, fatigue, and difficulty rising from a chair
Elevated alkaline phosphatase and PTH with normal or low calcium and phosphorus supporting metabolic bone disease
Exclusion of look-alikes such as hypothyroidism, fibromyalgia, polymyalgia rheumatica, and primary hyperparathyroidism
Consideration of rickets in children or osteomalacia in adults when severe

easy: Older adult with limited sun exposure and diffuse bone pain
Low 25-hydroxyvitamin D level with elevated alkaline phosphatase and PTH
Proximal muscle weakness and difficulty rising from a chair
Clear risk factors such as housebound status or dark skin at high latitude
medium: Exclusively breastfed infant with irritability and delayed milestones
Patient with malabsorption or bariatric surgery and nonspecific fatigue
Normal calcium and phosphorus despite low vitamin D
Symptoms attributed to aging or depression
hard: Child with rickets and skeletal deformity but no reported bone pain
Older adult presenting with falls or a fragility fracture without bone pain
Patient with obesity and mild symptoms despite markedly low vitamin D
Chronic kidney disease with bone pain and abnormal calcium and phosphorus
